newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina rejects post office bidding appeals.
newsitem.headline: Argentina rejects post office bidding appeals.

text.p: Argentina's state post office Encotesa said Tuesday it had rejected challenges from three groups who were disqualififed from the bidding for a 30-year concession to run the Argentine post office.
"Of the three groups who challenged, three have been rejected," said an Encotesa spokeswoman, adding that further details of the decision would be given later in the day.

Encotesa President Arturo Puricelli told reports that the appeals by a Dutch group headed by ING-Barings, local building company Roggio and a Brazilian group headed by airline VASP had all failed and they would lose their $500,000 deposits, which would have been reimbursed had they won.
"They knew the conditions," said Puricelli, shrugging off lobbying by foreign foreign embassies with firms involved and even reported threats of international writs.

Six groups put forward bids for Encotesa. The conditions included a $250 million investment plan over the first 10 years and annual investment of one percent over revenue from then on, and the technical support of an official post office recognized by the Universal Postal Union.
The winner would be whoever offered the government the highest fee, to be paid half-yearly and in advance.
But the privatization commission handling the sale ruled that three of the groups did not qualify.

"We disqualified three groups, because two of them didn't have the backing of their official post offices and in the other case there was no complete investment plan, to our judgment," said the Encotesa chief Tuesday.

"The position on the Roggio and ING Barings-Caiman groups is that we don't consider that the advisors to the Canadian and Dutch post office can be the technical operators foreseen in the prospectus, which talks about state official post offices," said Puricelli.
ING took Nepostel Consultancy NV as its postal operator while Roggio took Canada Post System Management Ltd. Encotesa said these are not official postal operators, but consultants.
The three groups that did qualify were:
- Local transport company TAC, with local group Roman and businessman Samuel Liberman, with Germany's state post office.
- Itron and Sideco, controlled by Argentina's Grupo Macri, and Argentina's Banco Galicia, with the British Post Office.
- Local banking group Werthein and COINTEL, a holding that controls Telefonica de Argentina, with New Zealand's Intratil International and New Zealand Post.
The final result of the bidding is scheduled for July 28.
